headline: US Consumer Sentiment Rises to 51.0 in November, Beating Expectations
summary: The University of Michigan US consumer sentiment index rose to 51.0 in November, beating expectations of 48.0. One-year inflation expectations declined to 4.3% from 4.7%.
why: US consumer sentiment data measures household spending optimism, a major component of US GDP.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: Beating consumer confidence estimates indicates ongoing resilience in private domestic demand.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Higher consumer sentiment and falling inflation expectations supported US equities late in the week.
